prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After reading the openings I move my first preference from halide perovskites (B068, which only Zou Xiaodong also ranked and only at seventh) to targeted protein degradation (B066). It is the one candidate that four of six supporters placed in their top four, and it also meets my own test: a clear underlying principle (induced proximity, where a small molecule forces a ubiquitin ligase and a target together so that the cell's own machinery destroys the target), quantitative mechanistic support from ternary-complex structures and degradation kinetics, and a genuinely new capability, since inhibitors need an occupiable active site and degraders do not. That is the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' criterion I apply as Chair. A prize for Crews, Deshaies and Handa also lets us tell a coherent story to a broad audience: the PROTAC concept and the discovery that thalidomide-type glues work through cereblon are two faces of one principle.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC or degrader drug is approved yet, so the committee would be recognising a mechanism and a platform ahead of clinical proof. The three-name cap forces us to leave out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a defensible claim, and Handa's cereblon discovery is closer to a molecular-glue story than to the PROTAC concept, which could make the citation look like two prizes squeezed into one. If the clinical readouts disappoint, the prize would age badly.

responses.point: Zou ranks B066 third but warns that approval and long-term impact are not yet complete, so recognition may be slightly premature, and that credit is crowded.
responses.response: I take the timing concern seriously, but I would separate the discovery from the product. The Nobel question is whether the principle is established and reproduced, and ternary-complex structures, cereblon biochemistry and the many independent degrader programmes show that it is. Waiting for approval would mean letting regulatory timelines, not scientific maturity, set our schedule. I do agree on crowding: we should keep the citation on the principle and not on any single drug, and I would like Zou's view on whether Handa or Ciulli better anchors the glue/ligase-recruitment side.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B038) first for Buchwald and Hartwig as a general, ligand-driven method that is overdue and has a clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: The attribution is indeed the cleanest on the shortlist and I rank B038 as my first alternative. My qualification is breadth of surprise: the 2010 cross-coupling prize already established the palladium oxidative-addition/reductive-elimination framework, so B038 reads as a major extension of a recognised concept, whereas degradation introduces a new pharmacological principle. If Somfai can show that C-N coupling is a distinct conceptual step and not an optimisation, I would be willing to move it up.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks massively parallel sequencing (B057) first and argues that the Cambridge Solexa chemistry, not the commercial platforms, deserves the honour, with overdue recognition and complete validation.
responses.response: I agree on impact and maturity and keep B057 as an alternative. My reservation is about what exactly was discovered: sequencing by synthesis is an enormous engineering and chemistry integration, and the 1980 prize and the committee's wish to avoid a dispute with Medicine make me want a sharper statement of the chemical invention. I also note that Aqvist ranks B066 last, at eighth, and I would like to hear whether his objection is clinical immaturity or the attribution.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B066 first as the conversion of the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a chemical design principle with a general tool for biologists and drugs in the clinic.
responses.response: I agree and would use his formulation in the citation. I would press one point: the argument must not rest on thalidomide's medical history, which overlaps with Medicine-type recognition. The chemical contribution is that a small molecule can reprogram E3 substrate specificity, and Chabes's point about its use as a general research tool is the best protection against the 'no approved drug yet' objection.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept recognition of degraders before the first approval.
Allocation of the three places among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and Gray; I have not resolved whether Ciulli should replace Handa.
Whether a two-part prize (for example B066 with B022 or B057) would be stronger than a single-topic prize, given the three-person cap.
My views on perovskites are partly from memory and the stability/lead issue is unsettled, so I treat B068 as a lower-priority option rather than discarding it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I am a Lund colleague of Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, but that does not touch any shortlisted laureate. My nanowire and thermoelectric work has no connection to B066.
